title: Netflix's Big Bet: One model to rule recommendations: Yesu Feng, Netflix
talk_summary: Netflix consolidated dozens of independently-built recommendation models into one transformer foundation model that learns a shared user representation, then lets downstream application models consume it as a subgraph, embedding lookup, or fine-tune. They report scaling-law gains and infrastructure consolidation, plus LLM-borrowed tricks like multi-token prediction and multi-layer representation.

takeaways.technique: Consolidate duplicated per-agent logic into one shared foundation layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of each use case spinning up its own model with duplicated feature/label engineering, they centralize user representation learning once and make downstream models thin layers on top.

takeaways.technique: Multi-token / multi-horizon prediction to reduce myopia
takeaways.what_they_do: They predict multiple future tokens/facets rather than just the next action, forcing the model to target longer-term outcomes and be robust to train/serve time shift.
takeaways.evidence_quote: force the model to be less myopic more robust to serving time shift... targets long-term user satisfaction

takeaways.technique: Multi-layer representation aggregation for stable state
takeaways.what_they_do: They aggregate hidden states across layers and time to produce a more stable user representation despite constantly changing input history.

takeaways.technique: Distill/adapt a shared base per downstream latency budget
takeaways.what_they_do: Downstream consumers either embed the foundation model as a subgraph, consume pushed embeddings, or fine-tune/distill it to meet strict latency requirements.

takeaways.technique: Prompt tuning via swappable soft tokens
takeaways.what_they_do: They plan to train small soft-token prompts that can be swapped at inference to make one foundation model behave differently per application, instead of separate models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: can we just train some soft tokens so that at inference time we can directly swap in and out the soft tokens to prompt the FM to behave differently
